items.text: In adults starting oral anticancer agents, does pharmacist-led follow-up, compared with usual oncology follow-up, reduce unplanned toxicity admissions and severe toxicity within 90 days, and what happens to relative dose intensity and adherence (by measurement method)?
items.intervention: Pharmacist-led follow-up: consultation, early telephone checks, review before supplies
items.outcome: Unplanned toxicity admissions and severe toxicity (primary); dose intensity; adherence by method
items.setting: Cancer centres and outpatient oncology services

items.text: What pharmacist time and money does such a service take, and what admission costs have been reported as averted?
items.population: Services providing pharmacist-led follow-up for oral anticancer agents
items.outcome: Pharmacist hours per patient; service cost; reported averted admission costs

finer: Feasible in four months with two pharmacists part-time and library support; interesting and relevant to the funding decision; novel only as a local synthesis; ethical with no participants.
summary: One effects question with harms as the primary strand, and one time and money question kept separate.
